text:
acme_engineer: Hey team — after the update yesterday our chat responses got much shorter and 'safer'. Examples below, and it's affecting product UX. Any idea what changed?

maria_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a before/after pair and the model + request id you used? We'll open a ticket.

acme_engineer: Sample: Prompt -> "Write a friendly onboarding email to a new user about features X, Y, Z."
Before (2 days ago):
"Hey Sam — welcome! We're excited to show you X..."
After (today):
"Welcome. See features X, Y, Z."
No request_id; using our integration with default SDK, model: redwood/gpt-medium, and we didn't set temp/top_p explicitly.

maria_support: Thanks — can you repro with an explicit curl so we can gather request IDs? Also include the full response headers if you can.

acme_engineer: Repro curl I ran:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium","input":"Write a friendly onboarding email to a new user about features X, Y, Z."}'
```
Response snippet (today):
"Welcome. See features X, Y, Z."

maria_support: Got it. I'm escalating to eng (cc @dan_eng, @nick_ml).

oncall-bot: deploy/rr-serve-20260311-1123 succeeded (canary 100% -> prod).

oncall-bot: change: sampling-profile: default -> conservative-safety-v2

dan_eng: Looking quickly at the rollout notes — the canary applied a new default sampling profile for hosted API responses named conservative-safety-v2. That profile sets temperature=0.0 and top_p=0.3 at the platform-level when customers don't override params. We accidentally flipped the config key that applies profile to previously-unset requests.

nick_ml: Confirming: for conversational/marketing prompts that used to inherit the old default (temp ~0.8), setting temp=0.0 will collapse diversity and produce terse replies. This matches the customer's symptom.

maria_support: Ok — what's the mitigation? Customer needs immediate fix and backfill for any impacted requests (they might want to re-generate content).

dan_eng: Short term: we can either rollback the sampling-profile flag in the config or set a hotfix so that 'no params' leaves sampling unset (fallthrough to per-model default ~0.8). I can push rollback to prod in the next 15m.

dan_eng: Hotfix plan (commands):
```bash
# rollback config flag that applied conservative-safety-v2 to empty sampling
infractl apply -f /configs/sampling/rollout-disable-conservative.yaml --env=prod --tag=rr-20260311-rollback
```

maria_support: Can you also add a simple customer workaround? Suggest they pass explicit params in their request while we roll back. Example to share with them:
```json
{"model":"redwood/gpt-medium","input":"Write a friendly onboarding email...","sampling":{"temperature":0.8,"top_p":0.95}}
```

acme_engineer: Appreciate the workaround. If you rollback, can you confirm we won't get a billing event or different model variant? We just need content parity.

dan_eng: Rolling back now. I'll post status. (deploy logs: rollout disabled, config reverted.)

oncall-bot: rollout rr-20260311-rollback applied to prod.

nick_ml: I re-ran the customer's prompt in prod after the rollback with the same curl (no explicit sampling) and the response matches the "before" style (longer, friendlier). So rollback worked.

maria_support: Great. I've notified the customer and provided the workaround snippet and ETA for a short postmortem. Ticket: SUP-2026-312.

acme_engineer: Thanks — can we get the postmortem details (root cause, timeline, and which rollout changed the platform default)? We need it for our compliance review.

dan_eng: Root cause summary we'll include in postmortem: a config key change in the hosted default-applicator logic caused sampling-profile conservative-safety-v2 to be applied to requests that previously relied on the model's implicit sampling defaults. The rollout ID that introduced the change: deploy/rr-serve-20260311-1123. Time window: 2026-03-11T11:23:00Z -> 2026-03-11T11:45:00Z (rollback at 11:58Z). Impact: some customers saw reduced generation diversity when they didn't explicitly set sampling params.

nick_ml: Follow-ups: (1) add automated test to detect sudden drops in per-customer response entropy on rollout, (2) make conservative-safety profile opt-in not applied to empty sampling settings, (3) surface a warning in dashboard if a model's effective sampling defaults change for an org.

maria_support: I'll track those in the support engineering backlog and assign owners. Closing loop with customer now.

acme_engineer: Appreciate the quick response and the rollback. We'll re-generate a few items and confirm.

maria_support: Thanks everyone. Filing postmortem draft and we'll attach logs + request IDs. :white_check_mark:
